summary: A parent, Po, is seeking childcare options for their three-year-old daughter, who only understands Chinese. The parent is now working full-time and needs a reliable childcare solution. The advisor, Espon, explains that while daycare centers are the most common form of early childhood education in the area, most are either Finnish-speaking or Swedish-speaking, with very few offering English or Chinese. The advisor suggests visiting the official website, www.spo.fi, and exploring the "Child Care and Education" section to find available options. The advisor recommends checking both public and private daycare centers, noting that there are approximately 170 public and 90 private centers. The parent is advised to look for English-speaking options, as this was not previously available. The next step is for the parent to review the options on the website and contact the relevant centers for more information.

questionnaire.Any Additional Information: The customer mentioned their daughter is three years old and needs a daycare solution since they are working full-time. They expressed a preference for English-speaking or Mandarin-speaking facilities, as their daughter understands only Chinese. They also inquired about the cost, deductibles, and availability of private daycare options.
